questions.question: Illustrate inheritance in Java. • The mechanism of deriving a new class from an old class is called Inheritance. • The old class is known as the base class(or super class or parent class), and the new one is called the subclass (or derived class or child class). • A subclass is a specialized version of a superclass. It inherits all possible instance variables and methods defined by the superclass and adds its own, unique elements. • To inherit a class, we should use the keyword extends.

What will be the value of a after the execution of the following code segment in Java. int a = -1; a = a >> 4; In Java, the signed right shift operator (>>) fills the higher-order bits with the sign bit (1 for negative values). The binary representation of -1 is all 1's in two's complement (for a 32 -bit int, it's 32 ones). Right shifting by any number of bits for -1 keeps all bits as 1 (since the sign bit is 1), so the value remains -1 Therefore, after a = a >> 4;, a is still -1 3.
